findings_for_integrator.title: benefit_catalog_conditions.cedar_policy_ref accepts dangling policy references
findings_for_integrator.why_not_fixed_here: Lives in backend/crates/benefit/** plus the shared collision roots backend/openapi/openapi.yaml and clients/**. This lane owns only backend/crates/platform/db/{src/lifecycle.rs,tests/**} and its evidence dir.
evidence: backend/crates/platform/db/migrations/0157_create_benefit_catalog.sql:116 — cedar_policy_ref TEXT NULL CHECK (cedar_policy_ref IS NULL OR char_length(cedar_policy_ref) <= 200). No FK, no existence check.
backend/crates/benefit/adapter-postgres/src/lib.rs:695-699 — the only validation is normalize_optional_text(condition.cedar_policy_ref, 200, "cedar_policy_ref"), i.e. trim + length.
A real registry exists and is not consulted: cedar_policy_catalog_entries (backend/crates/platform/db/migrations/0150_create_cedar_policy_staging.sql:8).

All 12 backend occurrences of cedar_policy_ref (benefit/application 2, benefit/adapter-postgres 8, 2 in tests) are storage/serialization only. The value is never resolved and never evaluated anywhere.
findings_for_integrator.impact: A benefit-catalog condition can be stored and rendered as policy-governed while pointing at a Cedar policy that does not exist. The condition then silently governs nothing, which is a fail-OPEN eligibility rule presented to operators as fail-closed. Contradicts DESIGN 3.10 (fail-closed, deny-by-default) and the typed-fields discipline in DESIGN item 19.
findings_for_integrator.suggested_fix: Resolve cedar_policy_ref against cedar_policy_catalog_entries inside the write transaction and reject unknown refs with the canonical validation envelope; or drop the column if the benefit conditions are not in fact Cedar-governed yet (D-5: dead code = delete). Either way the openapi.yaml schema note and the regenerated ts/kotlin/swift clients must follow.

findings_for_integrator.title: OPTIONAL: promote CHECKER_TRANSITIONS into lifecycle_transition_rules
findings_for_integrator.detail: The maker-checker set landed as a compiled constant in backend/crates/platform/db/src/lifecycle.rs rather than a lifecycle_transition_rules.requires_checker column, because migrations/** is a serialized collision root (a lane cannot take a ledger slot) and because a compiled preventive security control cannot be widened by a data change. The set is still declarative data, not a per-domain match arm.
findings_for_integrator.if_promoted: Needs one ledger migration slot: ALTER TABLE lifecycle_transition_rules ADD COLUMN requires_checker BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false; then UPDATE for ('document','submitted','approved') and ('benefit_catalog_item','pending','finalized'); then swap is_checker_transition() for a lookup. The existing tests cover the behaviour either way.
findings_for_integrator.recommendation: No action required. Only promote if the integrator wants the rule tunable per deployment.

findings_for_integrator.title: archived -> disposed is NOT gated as a four-eyes transition (open design question)
findings_for_integrator.detail: DESIGN 3.9.1 lists maker-checker under governance mechanisms common to create/change/dispose, but the gate it actually names for 폐지 is the 참조 무결성 게이트 / 정산 completeness, and the FSM has no 'dispose requested' state, so there is no recorded maker to compare a disposer against. Disposal stays gated on legal_hold + retention_until only. Inventing a second approver here would be the blanket same-actor ban the charter forbids.
findings_for_integrator.recommendation: Founder/design call: if 폐기 needs 결재, the FSM needs a dispose-request state first.

environment_notes.title: dev-PG console_buck_admin harness password was unset; one was set
environment_notes.detail: backend crate tests using #[sqlx::test] must satisfy migration 0196: CURRENT_USER = console_buck_admin AND startup option mnt.sqlx_test_bootstrap = buck-sqlx-superuser-v1. The role existed on the shared dev PG with no password. Set to console-buck-admin-local (dev-only, local-bound container).

environment_notes.title: shared dev Postgres crashed mid-lane on a full Docker volume
environment_notes.detail: The Docker VM volume backing console-dev-postgres-1 hit 197G/0 avail and Postgres entered a restart loop (FATAL: could not write lock file postmaster.pid). Cause was 684 orphaned anonymous docker volumes (~85GB) left by disposable Buck2 PG harness containers across lanes; PGDATA itself was 597MB. Escalated to main and cleared with docker volume prune. Recommend adding the prune to wave teardown.
